candidate.name: sequence length
candidate.meaning: The number of entries in the input and output sequences, the length of the transform; it is also the order of $\omega$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The order of the root, a positive integer that counts the positions of the transform it labels.

candidate.name: input index
candidate.meaning: The index of an input entry $a_j$, running from $0$ to $n-1$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: An integer exponent of the root, the smaller of two powers compared in the distinctness argument.

judged.note: On fourier-transform, the input index j clashes with the root exponent j of roots-of-unity. Use another letter for the input index (e.g. i), since j is the exponent of the root on the earlier page.

candidate.name: output index
candidate.meaning: The index of an output entry $\hat a_k$, running from $0$ to $n-1$.
candidate.earlier_meaning: An integer exponent of the root, marking which power of $\omega$ is meant.

judged.note: On fourier-transform, the output index k clashes with the root exponent k of roots-of-unity. Use another letter for the output index (e.g. h), since k is the exponent of the root on the earlier page.

candidate.name: digit width
candidate.meaning: The number of bits in one digit, so each digit lies between 0 and 2^b-1.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The second of the two input sequences, a list of r complex numbers.

judged.note: On convolution-reduction, the digit width b clashes with the second input sequence b of cyclic-convolution. Use another letter for the digit width (e.g. w).

candidate.name: coefficient count
candidate.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in the list of one element of the ring, a power of two.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The number of complex coefficients in each input sequence, so both sequences have length r.

candidate.name: input sequence
candidate.meaning: The sequence $x_0,\dots,x_{2r-1}$ of ring elements whose transform is taken.
candidate.earlier_meaning: The formal variable of $p$, a placeholder for a number to be substituted.

judged.note: On synthetic-transform, the input sequence x clashes with the formal variable x of the Fourier and cyclic convolution pages. Use another letter for the input sequence (e.g. u).
